Call for Sites to inform the variation of the County Development Plan 2023 – 2027

Destination and Experience Development Plan (DEDP) for Co Laois  
Fáilte Ireland has commissioned Consultants to prepare a DEDP for Laois in 2026. This 5-year

and maximize their chance at success.  
 
 The DEDP will focus on key priorities for the county including developing Irelands Ancient east

amenities and supporting Tourism business with sustainability, climate action, accessibility and 
marketing, amongst other key areas.

to initiate consultation on this important plan for the

Regenerative Tourism Update 
 
Making Tracks, a new low-carbon, slow tourism enterprise, has officially opened in 
Ballybrophy, Co. Laois, offering a unique visitor experience that includes glamping, horse-
drawn wagon tours, and an Irish country house hostel. 
 
The project was awarded €250,000 in funding through Fáilte Ireland’s Regenerative Tourism 
and Placemaking Scheme, which is co-funded by the Government of Ireland and the European 
Union through the EU Just Transition fund. This project will enhance the visitor experience and 
help to drive tourism across Co. Laois and the wider region. 
 
 
 
The Hyland Family together with Cathaoirleach Mr. Barry Walsh and Special Guest, Mr.  Eoin Reardon officially opened Making 
Tracks on the 12th September 2025. 
 
Opened by wood-craft restorer Eoin Reardon, the project involved the restoration of the former 
Ballybrophy House into an Irish Country House Hostel adjacent to the Ballybrophy train station, 
construction of 5 glamping units and the development of horse-drawn wagon experiences 
throughout south Laois. 
 
Accessibility and inclusivity were central to the project, with the development of universally 
accessible showers, pathways, and site access to ensure a welcoming experience for all visitors.

STEM passport for inclusion 
 
This is a recent addition to STEM learning. First rolled out by Longford County Council, Laois is 
now also an active collaborator. The STEM Passport for Inclusion is aimed at TY and 5th Year 
students with the goal of equipping them with knowledge of computational thinking, coding and 
Python programming.  
 
Upon successful completion, students will receive a Level 6 Certificate and 50 bonus points in 
their Leaving Certificate. These bonus points are accepted towards the CAO choices of STEM-
related courses in Maynooth University, TUS Athlone and MTU Cork, all of whom are our 
facilitators along with our STEM Engagement Officer. This is being rolled out in Mountmellick 
Community School and one other Laois secondary school to be decides on.  
 
 
 
 
WP 4 Midlands Ireland Placemaking 
Plans are well underway for the  Midlands Showcase event which is taking place in the TUS 
Athlone International Arena, Athlone, Co. Westmeath on Wednesday, 3rd December 
2025 from 10am to 4pm. 
  
This day-long event will feature an experiential exhibition of the Midlands as a place to live, 
work, and learn. It will also be divided into three stages: a main stage for panel discussions 
and two smaller stages called Innovation and Support, which will showcase everything the 
region has to offer.  Initiatives such as STEM Education and Sustainability will be central, 
as well as a Midlands Eco Village.   The Midlands Showcase website will be going live in the 
coming weeks.

Heritage 
 
 
Unveiling New Visitor Interpretive sign at Aghaboe Abbey 
 
On 11th October Her Excellency Melitta Schubert, Ambassador of Austria to Ireland 
unveiled a new visitor interpretive sign at Aghaboe Abbey. This project was supported 
with funding from the Heritage Office and Creative Ireland Laois. There is an historic 
link between Aghbaoe and Salzburg through Feargal (later St. Virgilius) who served as 
Abbot of Aghaboe and subsequently travelled to Salzburg founding a cathedral there in 
the 700s. 
 
The Heritage Officer worked closely with the Aghaboe Preservation Committee on the 
project. An Interpretive illustration of how the site might have looked in the year 1400 
was commissioned with historians and archaeologists consulted throughout the process 
to ensure details of the interpretive illustration and the information on the panel were 
as accurate as possible. 
 
In addition to Laois County Council staff and local representatives, the unveiling had 
great attendance by locals, and the event was followed by music and refreshments in a 
marquee set up in the carpark for the day. 
 
 
Attendees at the unveiling including Cathaoirleach Cllr Barry Walsh, Cllr Conor Bergin, Cllr John King, T.D. Willie Aird, 
Austrain Ambdassador Melitta Shubert, members of the Aghaboe Preservation Committee, David Broderick, Creative 
Communities Coordinator, Thomas Carolan, Heritage Officer, and Bernie Foran, County Foran.
